top_violation_types.title: Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3401(a))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operation did not have a current health inspection.

top_violation_types.title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Two infants did not have current infant feeding schedules.

top_violation_types.title: Adequate Lighting During Naptime (26 TAC §746.2911)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: In the 3 to 5 yr old classroom the room had inadequte light and the children were not visable. The caregiver could not see the children.

top_violation_types.title: AP Never exceed capacity of the home (26 TAC §747.207(10))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operation was observed caring for thirteen children. The capacity on the permit is 12.

top_violation_types.title: AP Initial background checks submitted - At the time a non-client resident 14 or older moves into your home or operation (26 TAC §745.621(a)(5))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: It was determined that the primary caregiver did not submit a background check for a household member.

top_violation_types.title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio (26 TAC §744.1601)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operation exceeded the maximum group size for two or more caregivers.

top_violation_types.title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §744.1205(a)(4))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Based on the information gathered during the investigation, it has been determined that child was left unattended, and caregiver was not at a physical proximity which did not allow visual and/or auditory awareness of the child in care.

top_violation_types.title: Children's Records - Admission Information (26 TAC §744.603(a)(2))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: 5 of the 6 children's files reviewed were missing the completed doctor or hospital information.  5 of the 6 children's records reviewed were missing the address of the emergency contact.
